disagreements: Wheat falling-number targets: IREKS 300-360 s normal; BAKERpedia 250-280 s industrial target; German Wikipedia 230-280 s normal and 200-250 s 'optimal'; Newberry 2018 found no baking penalty from late-maturity amylase at 157-294 s.
Rye falling number: IREKS 180-240 s normal vs Murniece (citing Kucerova) 125-200 s good; Wikipedia minimum 120 s.
α-amylase 'optimum': 40-60 C (BAKERpedia, dough) vs 72-74 C (Murniece, scald) vs 71-72 C (brewing).

Heat stability ranking vs numbers: BAKERpedia ranks fungal α-amylase as the least heat-stable source, yet Rebholz (citing Cauvain) gives about 80 C for fungal inactivation while IREKS gives 75 C for (cereal) α-amylase; no single source measured both.

nutrition.wording_rule: statements describe studies (population, dose, effect size, certainty); no advice, no promise
disagreements: Sourdough and glycaemia: Rolim 2022 meta-analysis reports a small pooled reduction (low/very low certainty, comparators include glucose) vs Starowicz 2026 (27 studies, insufficient) and EFSA 2014 (effect vs glucose not specific); Ribet 2023 counts mostly null comparisons in healthy people.

Fermentation time and fructans: longer proof lowered fructans in refined wheat (Schmidt 2021) but not in rye (Pejcz 2020); sourdough lowered rye fructans (Pejcz) yet left wheat total FODMAPs unchanged by adding mannitol (Schmidt).

Coeliac disease: experimental fully hydrolysed sourdough wheat (8 ppm, fungal proteases) was tolerated (Greco 2011) while ordinary sourdough is not gluten-free; the experimental process is not home or bakery sourdough.
